keyVerseText: And Jehu the son of Nimshi shalt thou anoint to be king over Israel: and Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abelmeholah shalt thou anoint to be prophet in thy room. Elisha: Gr. Eliseus
rootMeaning: The name אֱלִישָׁע (ʼĔlîyshâʻ) is a contracted form of אֱלִישׁוּעַ (ʼĔlîyshûwaʻ), which means "my God is wealth" or "God is salvation." This root meaning emphasizes a personal and divine provision or deliverance, highlighting God's role as the source of salvation and blessing. The literal sense enriches the common English gloss "Elisha" by embedding a theological affirmation of God's saving power within the name itself.
usageInScripture: The word אֱלִישָׁע appears 58 times in the Hebrew Bible, primarily as a proper name referring to the prophet Elisha, who succeeded Elijah. It is most frequently translated as "And Elisha" (18 occurrences), reflecting the narrative focus on his active role. Other common translations like "of Elisha" and "unto Elisha" indicate the relational and functional contexts in which the name appears, consistently pointing to the same prophetic figure. This consistency underlines Elisha's recognized identity and significance in the biblical text.
theologicalSignificance: The original meaning of אֱלִישָׁע as "God is salvation" is deeply significant for Christian faith, as it points to the central biblical theme of divine deliverance. Elisha, as a prophet named to embody this truth, serves as a living testimony to God's saving power among His people. Understanding his name reminds believers that God’s salvation is both personal and active, working through His servants to fulfill His covenant promises. This reinforces the believer’s trust in God as the ultimate source of salvation, a truth ultimately fulfilled in Christ.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Kings 19:16, the Lord commands the anointing of Elisha as prophet in Elijah's place, identifying him specifically as "Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abelmeholah." The use of the name אֱלִישָׁע here not only identifies the individual but also subtly proclaims the message that God is salvation. This highlights Elisha’s prophetic mission as one rooted in God's saving power, preparing the way for continued divine intervention and guidance for Israel.
